heading.en: Why ruby is red and emerald green

hook.en: Ruby and emerald both owe their *colour* to traces of Cr³⁺. The surrounding atoms split the d orbitals by different amounts, so each gem absorbs a different colour.
hook.kn: ಮಾಣಿಕ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ಪಚ್ಚೆ ಎರಡರ ಬಣ್ಣಕ್ಕೂ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ Cr³⁺ ಕಾರಣ. ಸುತ್ತಲಿನ ಪರಮಾಣುಗಳು d ಕಕ್ಷೆಗಳನ್ನು ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಪ್ರಮಾಣದಲ್ಲಿ ವಿಭಜಿಸುವುದರಿಂದ ಪ್ರತಿ ರತ್ನ ಬೇರೆ ಬಣ್ಣವನ್ನು ಹೀರುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Describe d-orbital splitting in octahedral and tetrahedral fields
Use the spectrochemical series to predict high or low spin

say.en: Ruby and emerald both owe their colour to traces of Cr cubed⁺. The surrounding atoms split the d orbitals by different amounts, so each gem absorbs a different colour. In this lesson: Describe d-orbital splitting in octahedral and tetrahedral fields.
Use the spectrochemical series to predict high or low spin.
Explain colour by d-d transitions.

body.en: Crystal field theory treats ligands as point charges that repel the metal's d electrons. In an octahedral field the two e_g orbitals (d_x²−y², d_z²), which point at the ligands, rise by 0.6Δo, and the three t₂g orbitals (d_xy, d_yz, d_xz) fall by 0.4Δo. Ligands can be arranged by the size of Δo they cause: the spectrochemical series. If Δo < P (pairing energy), electrons enter e_g first: high spin (weak field). If Δo > P, they pair in t₂g: low spin (strong field). In a tetrahedral field the *splitting* is reversed and smaller, Δt = (4/9)Δo, so tetrahedral complexes are high spin.
body.kn: ಸ್ಫಟಿಕ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ಸಿದ್ಧಾಂತದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಿಗ್ಯಾಂಡ್‌ಗಳು ಬಿಂದು ಆವೇಶಗಳು. ಅಷ್ಟಫಲಕೀಯ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ e_g ಕಕ್ಷೆಗಳು 0.6Δo ಮೇಲೆ, t₂g ಕಕ್ಷೆಗಳು 0.4Δo ಕೆಳಗೆ. Δo < P ಆದರೆ ಅಧಿಕ ಸ್ಪಿನ್; Δo > P ಆದರೆ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಸ್ಪಿನ್. ಚತುಷ್ಫಲಕೀಯದಲ್ಲಿ Δt = (4/9)Δo.

points.en: Spectrochemical series: I⁻ < Br⁻ < SCN⁻ < Cl⁻ < S²⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < C₂O₄²⁻ < H₂O < NCS⁻ < edta⁴⁻ < NH₃ < en < CN⁻ < CO
Δo > P: low spin; Δo < P: high spin
Δt = (4/9)Δo; tetrahedral complexes are high spin

title.en: On the board: crystal field theory

say.en: Six ligands approach along the axes. The two e g orbitals point at them and rise; the three t 2 g orbitals point between and fall.
In a tetrahedral field the order is reversed and the splitting is only four ninths as large.
Ligands in order of increasing field strength make the spectrochemical series.
For d four, if delta o is smaller than the pairing energy P the fourth electron goes up: high spin. If larger, it pairs: low spin.
Titanium three plus in water absorbs about 498 nanometres, blue-green light, and looks violet. That photon energy is delta o.
On the board: crystal field theory.

narration.en: Six ligands split the d orbitals into t2g (−0.4Δo) and eg (+0.6Δo). If Δo is smaller than the pairing energy P, electrons go up to eg before pairing (high spin). A d–d jump absorbs light of wavelength 1/Δo, and we see the complementary colour.
narration.kn: ಆರು ಲಿಗಂಡ್‌ಗಳು d ಕಕ್ಷಕಗಳನ್ನು t2g (−0.4Δo), eg (+0.6Δo) ಆಗಿ ವಿಭಜಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. Δo < P ಆದರೆ ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗುವ ಮೊದಲು eg ಗೆ (ಉನ್ನತ ಸ್ಪಿನ್). d–d ಜಿಗಿತ 1/Δo ತರಂಗಾಂತರದ ಬೆಳಕು ಹೀರುತ್ತದೆ; ಪೂರಕ ಬಣ್ಣ ಕಾಣುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: When visible light falls on a complex, an electron can absorb a photon of energy Δo and jump from t₂g to e_g (a d–d transition). The complex shows the complementary *colour* of the light absorbed. [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺ absorbs blue-green light near 498 nm and looks violet. Without ligands there is no splitting, so anhydrous CuSO₄ is white but CuSO₄·5H₂O is blue. Changing the ligand changes Δo and so the colour: green [Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺ turns blue and then violet as en is added.
body.kn: ದೃಶ್ಯ ಬೆಳಕನ್ನು ಹೀರಿ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ t₂g ಯಿಂದ e_g ಗೆ ಹಾರುತ್ತದೆ; ನಾವು ಹೀರಿದ ಬಣ್ಣದ ಪೂರಕ ಬಣ್ಣವನ್ನು ನೋಡುತ್ತೇವೆ. ನಿರ್ಜಲ CuSO₄ ಬಿಳಿ, ಜಲಯುಕ್ತ CuSO₄ ನೀಲಿ.

heading.en: Crystal Field Theory, Colour and Applications

tagline.en: d-orbital splitting in octahedral and tetrahedral fields, the spectrochemical series, high- and low-spin complexes, CFSE, colour, metal carbonyls and uses.

say.en: In a tetrahedral field the splitting is inverted (e below t₂) and smaller: $\Delta_t = \tfrac49\Delta_o$. It is almost never larger than P, so tetrahedral complexes are high spin.
[Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺ (d¹) absorbs at 498 nm (blue-green) and so appears violet. $E = hc/\lambda = (6.626\times10^{-34})(3.0\times10^{8}) / (498\times10^{-9}) = 3.99\times10^{-19}$ J per ion.

In Ni(CO)₄ (tetrahedral), Fe(CO)₅ (trigonal bipyramidal) and Cr(CO)₆ (octahedral), CO donates a lone pair to the metal (σ bond) and the metal donates d electrons back into empty π* orbitals of CO (π back bond). This synergic bonding strengthens M–C and weakens C≡O.

problem.en: Write the configuration and CFSE (ignoring pairing energy) of a d⁴ ion in (a) a weak octahedral field and (b) a strong octahedral field.

steps.en: (b) Δo > P: t₂g⁴ e_g⁰. CFSE = 4(−0.4) = −1.6Δo (plus one pairing energy P).
High spin has 4 unpaired electrons; low spin has 2.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Write the configuration and CFSE (ignoring pairing energy) of a d⁴ ion in (a) a weak octahedral field and (b) a strong octahedral field.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Write the configuration and CFSE ignoring pairing energy of a d to the power 4 ion in a a weak octahedral field and b a strong octahedral field.
a delta o is less than P: t 2g cubed e g to the power 1. CFSE equals 3minus 0.4 plus 10.6 equals minus 0.6delta o.
b delta o is greater than P: t 2g to the power 4 e g to the power 0. CFSE equals 4minus 0.4 equals minus 1.6delta o (plus one pairing energy P).
High spin has 4 unpaired electrons; low spin has 2.
So the answer is a t 2g cubede g to the power 1, minus 0.6delta o; b t 2g to the power 4, minus 1.6delta o plus P.

Energy per photon E equals hc/ lambda equals (6.626 times 10 to the power minus 34 times 3.0 times 10 to the power 8)/(498 times 10 to the power minus 9) equals 3.99 times 10 to the power minus 19 joules.
Per mole: 3.99 times 10 to the power minus 19 times 6.022 times 10 to the power 23 equals 2.40 times 10 to the power 5 joules mol to the power minus 1.
delta o is approximately 240 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1.
So the answer is delta o is approximately 240 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1.
